rounds.name: Round 1 Online Assessment
rounds.description: The First round (60 Questions) was the online assessment having 3 sections (No Negative Marking): Section 1 – Logical based thinking, Section 2 – English Language based, Section 3 – Technical Based covering OOP, DBMS, Computer Communication Networks, DSA etc.

rounds.name: Round 2: Technical Interview Round
rounds.description: 45‑60 minute interview focusing on depth of knowledge, resume, projects, situational questions, data analytics, cloud computing, DBMS, SQL schema design, queries, HAVING vs WHERE.

questions.text: Introduce yourself.
Explain your projects and work experience in depth.
Were these collaborative projects? If yes and a conflict arose then how would you manage it?
If some of your team mates were not on the same page then what would you do?
How would you approach people when you had to build a project on a tech stack that you don’t know?
What is cloud computing?
Design a schema for a School.
SQL Queries on the schema.
Difference between the HAVING and the WHERE clause.

rounds.name: Round 3 – HR Based Round
rounds.description: Purely HR based round with common questions, walking through resume, focusing on NGO experience and alignment with company values.

questions.text: Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
If not engineering then what will you be doing? And why?
One impression – good and bad that your friends will have about you? Why would they have that?
What do you know about General Mills?
Why choose General Mills?

tips.text: Questions might appear tricky. Since this will be the first section you will be attempting - the key part here is to balance your time as 15 minutes is less for this section. Go through all the questions and solve according to easiest to difficult strategy.
Section is straight forward with the basic level of English you will be able to crack this easily. Time is not an issue here, just have to think calmy.

Questions here were of easy to moderate level. A key part here is to take the smart guess when not sure. Some of them are objective based theory while some will be solving according to a data structure or so.
The best tip would be to remain calm and smile in this situation.

The key is to keep calm and have a smile on your face and then give the reply to best of your ability. Highlighting points relevant to the company is always beneficial as they see that your goals align with theirs.
Computer Fundamentals: Keep learning and practicing OOP, DBMS, DSA, and CCN.
Do your homework: Research the company you're interviewing with.
Be clear and confident: Focus on explaining your ideas clearly.
Be yourself: Honesty and authenticity are important in the HR round.
Know your stuff: Be ready to talk about your work experience projects and technical skills.
Format your resume: It is always a good practice to tailor your resume according to the company and the important points in your resume should be highlighted.

rounds.name: Round 1 Online Assessment
rounds.description: The online assessment round consisted of 60 questions and had a duration of 1 hour and 10 minutes. There were three sections: logical reasoning, language proficiency and technical questions.

rounds.name: Technical Round
rounds.description: Case study to design an app, discussing scalability, Firebase data storage, BCNF and normalization, and basics of microservices.

questions.text: Which subject excites me the most?
Design an app case study (requirements gathering, architecture, scaling from 3,000 to 30,000 users).
How to store large amounts of data using Firebase and handle scalability issues?
Explain concepts like BCNF and normalization.
Discuss basics of microservices.

rounds.name: HR- Based Round
rounds.description: HR interview covering personal introduction, family background, alternative career path, five‑year vision, friends' description, decision making, project brief, and motivation to join General Mills.

questions.text: Introduce yourself and share a bit about your family background.
If you hadn’t chosen engineering, what other career path would you have taken?
Where do you see yourself in the next five years?
How would your friends describe you?
What is the easiest decision you have taken so far in life?
What is the most difficult decision you have taken so far in life?
Explain one of your projects in brief.
Why do you want to join General Mills?

tips.text: Know your basic concepts: Be well‑versed in the fundamentals of CCN (Computer Communication Networks), OS (Operating Systems), DBMS (Database Management Systems), and Data Structures.
Aptitude practice: Practice sequences, patterns, and work‑related problems on various aptitude websites to sharpen your problem‑solving skills.
Focus on DBMS: Pay special attention to normalization in DBMS as it is a key concept often discussed.
Prepare for technical rounds: Be thorough with the projects mentioned in your resume and be ready to explain them in detail.
Master the basics: Ensure you have a strong understanding of core concepts, even in areas outside your projects.
Curiosity matters: If you're unsure about an answer, show curiosity and eagerness to learn more about it.
Be engaged and eager: Show genuine interest in whatever the interviewers explain and ask thoughtful follow‑up questions.
Stay confident: Maintain confidence throughout the interview, as it can leave a lasting impression.

rounds.name: Online Assessment
rounds.description: The online assessment round consisted of 60 questions and had a duration of 1 hour and 10 minutes. There were three sections: logical reasoning, language proficiency, and technical questions. The aptitude section consisted of 15 basic questions on topics like time-work problems and general math, to be completed in 20 minutes... The language proficiency section consisted of 15 questions in 15 minutes... The technical section included questions on object-oriented programming, computer networks, operating systems, SQL, and DBMS.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.description: The technical interview lasted 50 minutes to an hour, focusing heavily on my internship experience and projects, particularly in machine learning and web development... presented with a case study... The technical portion covered a range of topics: database choices, machine learning algorithms, specific SQL questions, neural networks, programming languages, favorite college subjects.

rounds.name: HR Interview
rounds.description: In my HR round, I was primarily asked personal questions, with a focus on my interests and experiences outside of academics... asked me to "sell" General Mills to them... committees and extracurricular activities... interests beyond my degree... future aspirations... reading habits... how my friends perceive me.

tips.text: To succeed in this selection process, focus on your core computer science fundamentals such as computer networks, object-oriented programming, operating systems, SQL, and aptitude.

For the technical interviews, ensure that you know your projects and internships thoroughly. Be prepared to discuss your contributions, the tech stack you used, and your reasoning behind specific choices. SQL and DBMS will often be revisited, so make sure to revise those topics, along with basic data structures and algorithms (DSA).

When it comes to the HR round, honesty, clarity, and genuineness go a long way. Research the company extensively before the interview so you’re ready to talk about it, and make sure you're prepared to discuss your interests outside of academics.
